Fine tuning is parameter efficient and conservative: a low learning rate and one epoch, to avoid overfitting the training domain. The system scores an F1 near 0.79 on unseen data on the leaderboard. The CodeBERT baseline manages only about 0.31.
arxiv-2606-25202:
Augmented reality overlays can feed a warehouse worker live information about a robot partner, but the graphics can also hide the real world at the wrong moment. Christian Fronk and three colleagues present ARTOO-DARTU, an AR system for warehouse human robot collaboration with an obstruction detection and mitigation pipeline built in.

The system shows situated analytics about the robot and accepts control input. It also watches for overlays that block important real elements, moving or fading them. For evaluation the team built Pocket MonstARs, a game like stand in for inventory picking where virtual monsters mark pick targets among labelled real boxes. In a study with 34 participants, the AR analytics raised task efficiency by 46 percent, but only with the mitigation pipeline active. Visibility preservation, not the analytics alone, made the gain.
arxiv-2606-25402:
Real projects pin old library versions while application interfaces keep changing, so a coding model must remember several versions of the same call at once. Daniele Cipollone and colleagues test that memory in 2026 with a benchmark spanning multiple releases of widely used Python libraries. Models face tasks where the right answer depends on the stated version, and a new consistency score grades their grip on software evolution. Errors that import a call from the wrong era are the telltale failure.

Leading models proved largely blind to versions: accuracy fell on changing interfaces while stable ones scored the same across releases. Merely naming the target version in the prompt did not help at all. Supplying the relevant documentation, by contrast, raised accuracy significantly. The authors call this a systematic weakness of training on corpora that mix all eras together.
arxiv-2606-25702:
Gravitational wave detectors hear the universe and their own creaks: glitches, brief instrumental transients that mimic cosmic signals. Luca Cirfeta presents DANTE in 2026, an unsupervised pipeline for the LIGO O4a run that hunts extended transients with no labels at all. A pretrained vision transformer reads time frequency spectrograms patch by patch, giving fine maps of odd structure. Controlled injections expose a signal dilution barrier: pooling methods that recover long, spread out shapes go blind to anything under a second.

An adaptive mixture model that picks its own covariance shapes steadies the clustering of glitch families, which otherwise shifts with small samples. Recalibrating the background on O4a data itself resolved a domain shift puzzle: morphologies first flagged as novel turned out to be stationary artefacts of the new run. Remaining lone anomalies, Cirfeta concludes, still need multi channel checks before anyone calls them real.
arxiv-2606-25802:
Alexander Mikhailov, Vladimir Novikov, and Jing Ping Wang classify integrable systems with two components. These are families of equations that admit endless chains of symmetries. Such systems matter across mathematical physics, but full classifications are rare even at low order. The team derives conditions for integrability that are both necessary and sufficient for polynomial systems of odd order in one space and one time dimension.

Exactly twenty-four spectral classes of such hierarchies turn out to be possible, sorted by their spectral invariants. The team also classifies all such homogeneous hierarchies whose lowest equations have order three and five. The list splits in two. C-integrable systems reduce by substitutions to a linear triangular form. S-integrable ones connect to canonical Drinfeld-Sokolov KdV-type systems. Those systems are tied to rank-two affine Lie algebras.
arxiv-2606-26002:
Kamar Hibatallah Baghdadi leads a team that shrinks neural networks with reinforcement learning. Compression mixes pruning, which cuts weights, and quantization, which lowers numeric precision. Searching both together by hand is slow. HiReLC splits the search into two levels. Low-level agents tune each block of the network on its own. They pick, per kernel, the bitwidth, how much pruning keeps, the quantization type, and its granularity.

High-level agents coordinate the whole budget. Ensemble voting guides them, informed by Fisher Information sensitivity scores. Policy checks are expensive, so a surrogate model steps in. A small neural surrogate predicts outcomes during an active learning loop. Fine-tuning after compression still gives the final verdict. On vision transformer and convolutional benchmarks, storage shrinks roughly sixfold. One setting even gains accuracy after compression. Other settings lose between about half a percent and five percent, a trade the team judges practical.
arxiv-2606-26102:
Juliana Seawell, Jasmine Brazilek, and Miles Tidmarsh ask whether teaching a model to be helpful can erode its values. Their test model is Llama 3.1 with eight billion parameters. It was mid-trained on synthetic data built around animal compassion. Standard post-training then follows, in helpfulness and coding flavours. Two methods, supervised fine-tuning and GRPO, deliver each flavour. Two benchmarks judge the damage: one on animal compassion, one on moral reasoning under uncertainty.

Helpfulness training does the harm. On the compassion benchmark, helpfulness-tuned models score far below coding-tuned ones under both methods. Moral reasoning on English items drops by a similar margin. The pattern refuses to travel, though. On multilingual moral reasoning, the domain effect vanishes entirely. Compassion behaves oppositely: its coding advantage grows larger on non-English items. The split suggests mid-trained values sit deeper and travel across languages better than late reasoning gains.
arxiv-2606-26202:
Nadine Fässler and Ben Moews ask whether mental health services leave a fingerprint on London crime. Their data join street-level crime records, mental health referral counts, and deprivation measures across Greater London. Statistical models and machine learning both mine the mix. A persistent positive link appears between crime rates and referrals, with referrals standing in for service access. The shape of the link surprises, though.

U-shaped is the pattern. At low service levels, more access tracks with prevention, as the standard hypothesis hopes. At high referral rates, demand driven by crime exposure seems to dominate instead. Explainable AI tools split the picture by crime category. A cluster analysis sorts boroughs into four types, each mixing crime, access, and deprivation differently. One-size policy fits none of them well. The study is among the first full treatments of the question inside Britain's public health system.
arxiv-2606-26302:
Evgeny Skvortsov and Richard van Dongen compute holographic correlators for Yang-Mills theories under several boundary conditions. Holography, through the AdS/CFT correspondence, equates a gravity-side theory with a boundary quantum theory. Boundary conditions decide which boundary theory a given bulk theory matches. The authors consider fixed-value, fixed-flux, mixed, and self-dual choices.

Three gauge theories are treated: ordinary Yang-Mills, its Chalmers-Siegel variant, and self-dual Yang-Mills. The authors derive the propagators, the building blocks of calculations, in various gauges for each boundary condition. They then compute three- and four-point correlators, the basic observable quantities, in all three theories. Comparing the results establishes how the observables relate across theories and boundary choices. The study is a companion to earlier work by the same authors.
arxiv-2606-26402:
Pratyusa Datta tackles a known headache in evolutionary biology: the rate of molecular change seems to depend on the timespan sampled, which distorts reconstructed family trees. His answer lets the substitution rate vary smoothly along a tree's branches.

Datta models the log rate as a smooth curve built from cubic spline pieces, with a prior that keeps it from wiggling wildly, and integrates it efficiently along branches. Simulations show the spline clock recovers true changing rates more accurately, with tighter credible intervals, than rival clock models. Applied to foamy virus and to SARS-CoV-2 spread across Europe, it finds strong time-varying signal in both.
arxiv-2606-26502:
Han-yu Wang compares how people and large reasoning models divide their effort across problems. Both take longer on harder problems overall. Within a single problem, though, the patterns point in opposite directions. A reasoning model spends more tokens, its units of generated text, on problems it gets wrong. People spend less time on the trials they fail.

Wang separates two levels of deliberation. Registration is how effort tracks difficulty across problems. Allocation is whether effort leans toward failures or toward successes. On a matched public corpus, people and five reasoning models agreed on registration. They diverged sharply on allocation, with every model showing a large wrong-versus-right effect. Wang reads the human pattern as engagement versus giving up. The model pattern looks like chains lengthening under uncertainty.
arxiv-2606-27102:
Ferrer and colleagues model the many-body behaviour of doped graphene nanoribbons, atom-thin carbon strips with extra charge carriers added. The chemical potential, the energy level up to which states fill, sits inside the bulk bands here. Both an extended and a simpler on-site Hubbard model describe interacting electrons on the ribbon lattice. In 2026, an exact mapping converts either model into a Kanamori model.

Kanamori form adds ferromagnetic exchange, which favours aligned spins, plus pair-hopping terms to the interaction picture. All Coulomb matrix elements, the strengths of electron repulsion terms, come out analytically. Their scaling with ribbon width and length is pinned down. A low-energy trimmed version then targets responses to outside fields. With proposed ribbon parameters, the model yields open-shell high-spin states. Those states can produce shell- and spin-blockade effects, where current flow stalls for spin reasons.
arxiv-2606-27202:
Bahi surveys graph neural networks, models that learn from data wired together as networks of nodes and links. Spectral and spatial formulations are derived from common first principles. Expressive power is tied to the Weisfeiler-Leman hierarchy, through precise statements of what today's architectures can and cannot tell apart. Twelve application domains are then examined in this review from 2026, from drug discovery to climate modelling.

Each domain gets its graph-building choices, costs, and dominant architecture families. Reported gains are separated from artefacts of weak baselines or lucky data splits. Cross-domain patterns recur: mixed-neighbour graphs and sheer scale undermine the same models almost everywhere. Time-changing graphs stay harder than static ones, and leaderboard winners rarely reach deployment. Over-smoothing, robustness, fairness, and explainability are treated as adoption constraints throughout. Claims for graph foundation models are judged suggestive, not settled.
arxiv-2606-27702:
Slater's list collects striking identities of Rogers–Ramanujan type. Each one sets an infinite series equal to an infinite product. Many have analytic proofs. What the series sides mean in terms of partitions is often far less clear. Aritram Dhar, Ankush Goswami, and Runqiao Li use Andrews' theory of separable partition classes in 2026 to give that meaning for more entries on the list.

The team builds one strict class of overpartitions and two families with gap rules on positions. In these families, bars over parts may appear only at alternating places. Their generating functions, which count the partitions in refined ways, match the series sides of seven of Slater's identities. With Heine-type transformations and Watson's q-analogue of Whipple's theorem, the product sides are recovered. A new companion identity and a signed companion formula are derived. The work shows these classes turn hypergeometric series into partition counts.
arxiv-2606-27902:
Ramanujan's mock theta functions hide striking patterns in their coefficients. Manosij Ghosh Dastidar studies the third order function rho in 2026. Its series coefficients appear to follow a strict sign law by index modulo three. Coefficients at multiples of three look positive. The next two residue classes look non-positive. Numerical evidence supports the pattern. The paper proves an asymptotic form of the law.

Watson's relation connects rho to another mock theta function, omega. A Rademacher-type expansion gives omega's coefficients precisely. A matching expansion handles a theta–eta product. Combining them yields the asymptotic formula for rho's coefficients. The leading constants differ by residue class in sign exactly as the law requires. One class has a positive constant, and the other two have negative constants. The sign law therefore holds for all sufficiently large indices. Whether it holds for every index remains open.
arxiv-2606-28002:
Insurance fraud raises premiums and erodes trust. Catching it when a claim first opens is a persistent challenge. Muhammad Shakeel Akram and four colleagues build a detection pipeline in 2026 that uses both text and voice. Existing work relies on private, text-only datasets. Their data are synthetic, so no real customer is exposed. The setup copies real claim calls. It creates dialogues between agent and customer, plus two-speaker audio.

Software transcribes the calls and separates the speakers. Later modules pull out names and patterns, search with a language model, and embed each voice. A rule-based risk score then flags problems. It catches reused stories, structural mismatches, and the same voice turning up across cases. Checks on the data and on each part show the system is stable. The design balances catching fraud against false alarms. It offers a baseline that others can reproduce, beyond text-only detection.
arxiv-2606-28202:
Md Niaz Imtiaz and Naimul Khan aim to recognize emotions from brain-wave recordings. The task breaks down when a system trained on one group of people or one dataset is used on another. Privacy rules often block sharing the original training data, so adaptation must work without it.

Imtiaz and Khan combine three ideas. The first is self-supervised pretraining that learns by predicting brain signals over time. The second is a two-stage adaptation that clusters the new data while tolerating noisy guessed labels. The third is light retraining at test time for uncertain cases. Across the DEAP, SEED, and DREAMER datasets, their method beat rival source-free approaches. Accuracy reached about seventy percent on SEED and sixty-three percent on DREAMER when starting from DEAP.
arxiv-2606-28402:
Shanfeng Zhang, Bo Gou, Yue Cao, Lei Zhang, Zhang Yi, and Tao He segment tiny objects in medical images, where sparse lesions drown in background and their borders blur. Global networks scanning the whole scan at once often miss such micro-targets or trace their edges badly, a serious flaw when the target is an early lesion.

Zhang and colleagues propose DCSNet, which turns the job into local refinement. A detection stage proposes regions and crops around them hierarchically, filtering out most background and easing the class imbalance. Inside those purified windows, a multiscale module blends transformer context with pixel-adaptive fusion to keep fine detail and sharp borders. Across three diverse medical datasets, DCSNet beat existing state-of-the-art methods by substantial margins, especially in boundary precision.
arxiv-2606-28502:
Gláuber C. Dorsch, Lucas P. C. Leão, Lucas M. B. Alves, Luiz C. A. Miranda, and Beatriz M. D. Sena stress-test a rescue plan for Starobinsky inflation, a leading model of the early universe. New microwave and galaxy data strain the model's predictions, unless reheating, the epoch right after inflation, was dominated by a stiff fluid. Stiffness, however, tilts the primordial gravitational-wave spectrum upward.

Dorsch's team examines three reheating histories mixing stiff, matter-like, and radiation eras. In every case, the parameter region favored at one-sigma confidence by the new data is already excluded by limits on extra radiation during Big Bang nucleosynthesis. Much of the looser two-sigma region would make gravitational waves loud enough for future detectors, from LISA to the Einstein Telescope, to hear, rendering the scenarios testable rather than merely embattled.
arxiv-2606-29002:
Hu, Appelo and Cheng design faster numerical schemes for open quantum systems, whose evolution follows the Lindblad equation. Simulating quantum hardware is hard because the density matrix, which describes such systems, is huge, and schemes must preserve basic physical properties. Their earlier work built a nested Picard iteration method of arbitrary order that is low-rank and completely positive and trace preserving, meaning it never produces unphysical states.

The new Gregory schemes swap expensive Gaussian quadrature rules for Gregory-type quadrature on evenly spaced nodes. They reach order up to nine while cutting computational cost substantially compared with the earlier method. Accuracy and structure preservation are retained. The team analyse stability on a physics-based test equation, and numerical experiments verify the convergence rate. Experiments also show the low-rank approximation working well, and they study a CNOT gate's performance in both closed and open quantum systems.
arxiv-2606-29102:
Al Shafi, Khan Zunayed, Ahmmed, Hossain, Mephu Nguifo and colleagues build BTI-Net, a network that learns medical image segmentation and classification together, letting the two tasks talk at every stage. Most multi-task designs share only the encoder, so each decoder rebuilds its output from private features. Boundary cues useful for classification and semantic hints useful for segmentation are then permanently lost to the other branch.

BTI-Net adds two-way communication at every decoder level through task interaction modules. Boundary context enters the classification branch through a gate, while global semantic priors scale the segmentation decoder, moving from coarse meaning to fine boundaries across four resolutions. An uncertainty proxy module gates each interaction per image and level, using alignment, complexity and confidence signals, with no extra annotations. On ultrasound, skin and brain MRI benchmarks, the net beat rival baselines on segmentation overlap and classification accuracy.
arxiv-2606-29502:
Tu and colleagues improve how AI agents use skill memories, stored textual guidance drawn from past experience. Such skills can help in one state yet mislead the same policy in another. Treating a skill-conditioned prompt as a fixed teacher is therefore fragile. Their framework is called UCOB, short for a credit-aware on-policy bidirectional self-distillation method.

UCOB compares two views of the same model on the same task and anchor state: one prompt with a skill, one without. Whichever view earns the higher return becomes the local teacher for that moment. This credit signal internalizes useful skill behaviour, corrects misleading skill use, and guides memory updates, retrieval choices, and reflection training. Tests cover ALFWorld, WebShop, and Search-QA tasks. UCOB beats skill-free reinforcement learning, skill-memory baselines, and other self-distillation methods across model scales, with gains over top baselines above twenty points on ALFWorld.
arxiv-2606-29802:
Suzuki and Yokoyama revisit Gödel's second incompleteness theorem, the result that a strong enough formal theory cannot prove its own consistency. Their note generalises the theorem from two directions and studies the ground around it.

One direction links how complex a theory's definition is to whether the theory can prove its own soundness. The authors clarify how this interacts with induction axioms, the rules that license proof by step-by-step ascent. They also pin down the exact logical strength of Craig's trick, a standard device for rewriting a theory's axioms. The other direction is semantic. They give a new unified proof of the versions where having a model is replaced by having special omega-models or beta-models.
arxiv-2606-30002:
Doyoung Choi and Jinhyung Park make a normality theorem for secant varieties fully effective. Secant varieties are built from lines joining points of an embedded variety. Earlier joint work showed the first two secant varieties are projectively normal. That held when the embedding line bundle was positive enough. The open part was saying exactly how positive is enough.

Choi and Park now give explicit effective conditions on the bundle. Their conditions guarantee projective normality for both secant varieties. They also treat the defining equations of the first secant variety. Under their conditions, that ideal is generated by cubic equations. More strongly, it is generated by three by three minors of a matrix. The matrix in question consists of linear forms. This sharpens an earlier theorem of Agostini and Park into effective form.
arxiv-2606-30102:
Le-Ji Xue and six colleagues study how two distant magnetic modes can be made to move in sync. Their system couples two optical whispering-gallery resonators. Each resonator also couples to a yttrium iron garnet sphere. That coupling links light to magnons, the magnetic excitations inside the spheres. A phase-dependent photon hopping term connects the two resonators.

The hopping phase gives a simple knob for controlling synchronization. Sweeping it from zero to pi transforms the magnon motion. Trajectories evolve from weak correlation to a highly synchronized state. Synchronization error drops significantly along the way. The authors check complete, phase-shifted, and quantum phase synchronization measures. Stronger photon hopping improves every synchronization measure they track. Thermal fluctuations, in contrast, weaken the coherent correlations behind sync. The results suggest a route to coherent control of collective magnon dynamics.
arxiv-2606-30202:
Jérémy Rieussec and Fabian Bastin survey how trust-region methods should update the radius that limits each step. These methods minimize a local model inside a ball of set radius. Good steps expand the radius; bad steps shrink it. Many update rules exist, with scattered convergence guarantees. In their 2026 survey, the authors isolate three structural conditions that unify them.

The conditions bound the radius below by the gradient size. They require contraction after unsuccessful iterations. They allow only controlled expansion after successful ones. Weak admissibility combines the first two conditions. It already forces the gradient norm to vanish eventually. Strong admissibility swaps in controlled expansion and yields optimal complexity. That bound governs worst-case steps to first-order stationarity. Five mechanism classes are verified against the conditions. Retrospective updates are newly proved convergent under growing model Hessians.
arxiv-2606-30602:
Kunyang Li, Kyle Domico, Jonathan Gregory and Patrick McDaniel ask where defenders of multi-agent systems should spend scarce security effort. In these systems, AI agents pass messages along communication channels. A compromised channel can poison the whole workflow, yet risk is uneven: one channel alone accounted for up to three quarters of total attack success in their observations.

Their framework, MESA, ranks channels by security criticality before any attack is seen. It needs no attack traces. Instead it combines six graph-theoretic metrics with two active probes, ablation and masking, that test how much each channel matters. Tested against a live misinformation attack across three scenarios, eight network layouts and five open models, MESA rankings tracked real per-edge attack success closely. Guarding only the top tenth of ranked channels intercepted about three times as many attacks as random placement.
arxiv-2606-30702:
Federico Felizzi builds a health benchmark from wearable motion data. Clinical medicine runs on structured tables, yet standard benchmarks for tabular learning ignore how real health data are gathered: complex survey sampling, deliberate oversampling of some groups, and fairness demands across subgroups. His benchmark draws on the United States NHANES survey from 2003 to 2006, with hip-worn accelerometry for thirteen hundred eighty-one adults.

Participants also gave fasting lab results, diet records and body measurements. Three methods, from ridge regression to the tabular foundation model TabPFN v2, predicted blood-sugar, triglyceride and inflammation markers from activity patterns and lifestyle inputs. TabPFN v2 performed best overall, explaining a fair share of the inflammation marker's variation. Triglycerides stayed largely unpredictable from lifestyle alone for every model. Ninety-percent prediction intervals, built with conformal methods, hit their coverage target for the predictable outcomes but fell short for some subgroups.
arxiv-2606-30802:
Mengyuan Xiao and colleagues present a spectroscopic census of the two hundred most massive galaxies seen in the universe's first two billion years. Massive galaxies stress-test formation theories, but a statistical spectroscopic view across cosmic time was missing. The sample, drawn from public James Webb telescope observations, covers redshifts from about three to fifteen and holds the top three percent most massive systems in the archive.

The team fitted each galaxy's spectrum and photometry together to derive masses and other properties, after removing contaminating red compact sources and broad-line active nuclei. The selection proved broadly robust to modelling choices. Populations shifted strongly with redshift: clean star-forming galaxies dominated early, while dusty star-formers and quiescent galaxies grew common later. Dust fell steadily toward higher redshift. Twenty-nine massive quiescent galaxies appeared, including some whose star formation had crashed within the past hundred million years.
arxiv-2606-30902:
Jiarui Li and six colleagues present TCR-SRIM, a model that predicts whether a T cell receptor will bind a given epitope, the fragment the immune system inspects. Such predictions guide immunotherapy design. But models often fail on epitopes they have never seen, and their reasoning stays opaque. TCR-SRIM combines protein language model representations with interpretable contact prototypes, learned example patterns that expose which residues drive a prediction, and adds a structural check to keep those patterns honest.

On the TCR-XAI benchmark it reached state-of-the-art predictive performance with better explanation quality. The team then used its transparency to audit generated structures. Structures predicted by AlphaFold3, TCRModel2 and tFold-TCR scored competitively yet produced less accurate interaction patterns and less diverse binding sites than real experimental structures.
arxiv-2606-31002:
Ke Zhang and five colleagues argue that compiling is not the same as translating faithfully, for turning mathematical English into Lean code. A generated Lean statement can type-check while dropping hypotheses, shifting domains or stating something vacuous. The team study faithful statement translation on a graduate-level benchmark of 400 entries spanning topology, algebra, and real and complex analysis. Their protocol combines Lean compilation, cross-model judging of meaning and human expert calibration.

A full tool-augmented agent compiled 89.5% of entries but reached only 60.5% consensus faithfulness. Human audits backed the metric: 96% of the outputs the judges passed were confirmed faithful, while 82.4% of compile-pass outputs they failed were confirmed failures of meaning. A structured study of three pipeline ingredients found elaboration feedback the largest validity lever, search mainly improving grounding, and fine-tuned drafting largely replaceable once both were present.
arxiv-2606-31102:
McCarthy, Amarasiri, and Gong build a tool for spotting research that is close to commercial use. Universities, funders, and investors want that signal early. Patents, licenses, and startups only appear years after a paper comes out. The team instead reads the paper's own words. Their Translation Readiness Index scores how similar a paper's text is to papers that later showed up in patent-paper pairs.

The team trained the index on 20,610 publications from OpenAlex. They turned titles and abstracts into semantic embeddings with SPECTER2. An XGBoost classifier then estimated the chance that a paper belongs to the patent-paired class. Patent-paired papers used more invention-oriented language. High scores also lined up with outside signs of translation, such as patent authorship and industry coauthorship. The index measures closeness to patented science, not proven commercial success.
arxiv-2606-31202: This author incentivizes data trading via profit reallocation. The incentivizing incentivizes. Their incentivizing is data trading profit reallocation. The incentivizing incentivizes. It is economics. The incentivizing is via. The data trading incentivizes profit-reallocated. The trading incentivizing is economic. The data trading is incentivized.
arxiv-2606-31402:
Wang studies when two kinds of models for representations of GL6 agree. Over a non-archimedean local field of characteristic zero, the Ginzburg-Rallis model arises by Whittaker induction from trilinear models for three copies of GL2. Whether the induced model equals the trilinear model of the inducing data was open in the case at hand.

Wang gives sufficient conditions for the Ginzburg-Rallis models of representations induced from a parabolic subgroup of a stated block type to be isomorphic to those trilinear models. A nonvanishing criterion for both families of models comes with the result. The work sits in the relative Langlands programme, where such model comparisons track how periods and L-functions should match across groups of different sizes.
arxiv-2606-31702:
Vasudevan, Somasundaram and Narayanan survey list-coloring, a generalization of graph coloring where each vertex carries its own list of allowed colors. A graph is chromatic-choosable when its list chromatic number equals its ordinary chromatic number. The topic began with work by Vizing and by Erdős, Rubin and Taylor in the 1970s, and the last full survey dates to 2001.

Coverage spans graph classes where equality is known and classes where a real gap appears. Embedded graphs, perfect graphs, bipartite and multipartite graphs, claw-free graphs, line graphs and graph products all receive treatment. The authors also review the main proof methods and several variants of list-coloring. Open conjectures about which classes are chromatic-choosable organize much of the discussion.
arxiv-2606-31802:
Gelastopoulos shows how lopsided selectivity in two-sided matching can arise from the matching process itself. In many bipartite networks one side can afford to be picky while the other must accept poor matches. Explanations usually point to traits of the two sides or to outside factors. Gelastopoulos instead models the feedback between them.

Individuals repeatedly form one-to-one matches and adjust their selectivity to hit a target matching rate. When encounters are frequent enough, analysis and simulation give one unique equilibrium: one group ends highly selective, the other non-selective. The split appears even when the groups' target-rate distributions overlap almost completely. Dating, hiring and housing markets are named as settings where the mechanism could apply.
arxiv-2606-31902:
Huisman and three others show that gradients of charged polymers generate their own electric field, and that the field speeds up small particles moving through it. Such gradients arise in drying paint and in breath droplets as they dry, full of mucin. Charged microparticles were thought to drift by chemiphoresis and diffusiophoresis alone.

Theory predicts a macroscopic field from charge separation: polymer and counterions move at unlike mobilities under a steady diffusive drive, so charge splits until a field builds to resist it. Experiments confirm the field is present. It much raises the phoretic velocity of the microparticles in their tests. For long polymer chains, propulsion turns gradient-independent, matching diffusiophoretic predictions for asymmetric electrolytes.
arxiv-2606-32002:
Alimaskina and five colleagues, at BRAIn Lab and Yandex Research, probe a hidden weakness in teaching language models from self-generated question-answer pairs. A model reads a document, invents questions about it, answers them, and the pairs become training data. That generation step quietly acts as a policy: it chooses which evidence becomes signal and decides how the evidence gets answered.

Coverage levels off quickly and gathers around the most prominent passages, with varied prompts ending up asking about the same passages, while messy markup can steer what gets asked. Answering models also obey instruction-like passages embedded in the source text. When each generated question is anchored to a fixed target, the selection of evidence becomes less biased. Filtering instruction-like spans before answering cuts mean injection compliance from 88 percent to 13 percent in their evaluation.
arxiv-2608-00102:
Ahmed and co-authors test whether LLM agents can price well in live markets. Agentic commerce is moving from concept to deployed infrastructure. Payment networks, retailers, and AI platforms set the stage for agent transactions. Real markets hide customer preferences and shift demand without warning. Competitors also adapt in real time.

Their Bazaar benchmark models dynamic sealed-bid auctions with multiple attributes. Closed-form customer utilities allow exact scoring. Eleven frontier models from four providers were tested. Leaders on customer acquisition were often not leaders on profit. Demand shocks reshuffled the rankings again. Fast pre-shock learners were often slowest to revise beliefs after a shock. Even the best agent captured under a third of hindsight-optimal profit.
arxiv-2608-00402:
Lyu and co-authors present DSETA, a dual-stage continual learning framework for travel time prediction. Arrival estimates anchor intelligent transport systems and ride-hailing platforms. Traffic patterns in large cities shift fast and irregularly. Past methods fail to adapt, or tangle long trends with short fluctuations. DSETA updates in stages to split those scales.

An intra-day stage learns from real-time data alone for short-term shifts. Events, holidays, and accidents fall in its scope. An inter-day stage uses short-window history for long distribution shifts like seasonal trends. A consolidation module guards regular patterns against catastrophic forgetting. Offline and online tests ran on DiDi platform data. A/B tests in Beijing, Wuhan, and Xi'an cut MAE by up to 6.62 percent. The system now serves hundreds of millions of daily requests.
barbara-blomberg-volume-02:
Barbara Blomberg steps forward in Volume 2 of the novel by Georg Ebers, set in Reformation era Germany. Ebers shows the young singer's father dusting off a sealed wine flagon for the knight Wolf, the man who loves her. Barbara's proud talk of a fairer fate has left Wolf certain he must win her, even if she can be his only briefly in this volume.

Chapter VI then tests that high picture of her within the hour. She throws down her smoothing iron, piles the finished work, and rolls up a length of ruby velvet without a glance at the parchment holding Wolf's verses. Off she goes to help poor Ursel and show off the fine cloth. Ambition, temper, and a working girl's errands cut across the romance her admirer is busy building.
bell-anatomy-brain-1802:
Charles Bell mapped the brain in The Anatomy of the Brain, from 1802, with engravings of rare beauty. The Scottish surgeon traced the nerves that carry feeling apart from those that move muscle. That split, sensory against motor, remade the study of the nervous system from the ground up.

Bell drew and engraved many plates with his own skilled hand. His findings guided surgery and physiology for the century that followed him. Clear prose makes hard anatomy open to the careful reader. The book founded modern neuroanatomy in effect, and its plates still draw praise from doctors and artists alike.
bellingshausen-forschungsfahrten-suedlic:
Fabian von Bellingshausen sailed for the far south in 1819 with two Russian ships and orders to push past all prior tracks. His account, in the German edition of 1902, tells that voyage of 1819 to 1821. His ships were the first to sight the mainland of Antarctica.

Six chapters run from Kronstadt out to the ice, along the new-found coast, and home again. Bellingshausen tells of storms, ice fields, new islands, and the hardships of his crews in plain naval prose. The sighting of a new continent gives the book its lasting rank. It is the record of one of the great firsts of exploration.
bennett-anna-five-towns-1902:
Arnold Bennett grew up in the Staffordshire Potteries, the five towns that fill much of his fiction. Anna of the Five Towns, published in 1902, was the novel that first made his name. It draws closely on the strict chapel world he knew as a young man.

Anna Tellwright inherits money of her own, yet her miserly father keeps tight control of her life. She must choose between a dutiful engagement and a love she truly feels. Bennett shows the cost of saving, duty, and gossip in a small industrial town. The novel remains a key work of English regional realism.
boguet-discours-des-sorciers-french-1602:
Henri Boguet was a judge in Franche-Comté who tried and burned witches himself. His Discours des sorciers of 1602 turns that courtroom experience into a book. Boguet writes in French for the judges and officials who would follow him in such cases.

He describes sabbaths, marks, and confessions drawn from his own trials. Attached stands his Instruction for a judge in witchcraft matters, a working manual in miniature. The tone is calm, methodical, and utterly convinced. Firsthand persecution is here codified for later hands. Few books bring a modern reader closer to the mind of a witch judge at work.
browne-literary-history-of-persia-vol-1-:
Edward G. Browne, the Cambridge orientalist who gave his life to Persia, opened his Literary History of Persia in 1902. This first volume runs from the earliest times to Firdawsi, the poet of the Shahnameh. It is still the classic English survey of Persian letters. The title page is missing from this scan, but the text is complete from the preface.

Browne moves from the Avesta and the inscriptions of kings through the Arab conquest to the rebirth of Persian verse. Rudaki, Daqiqi, and Firdawsi close the arc, with long extracts in his own translation. He writes as a lover of the land as much as a scholar. Every later student of Persian Sufi poetry starts in Browne's garden.
burnet-telluris-theoria-sacra-1702:
Thomas Burnet builds a sacred theory of the earth in Telluris Theoria Sacra, in Latin in this 1702 printing. The earth begins smooth as an egg, cracks at the Flood, and will end in fire. Newton admired the vast scheme, while theologians attacked its bold handling of Scripture and nature alike.

Mountains are ruins, in Burnet's striking view, the wreck of a fairer world. Poetry and geology blend in his grand, flowing Latin periods throughout. He sought to wed Moses to the new science of his age. The book founded geological theorizing in the English world, and its vision haunted writers from Milton's heirs to the Romantics.
cia-0000008702:
June 1973 brought a summary of photo comparison analysis results, looking back across many cases at once. The CIA's specialists had spent years matching prisoner photographs against missing-person files. A summary could judge the method itself: how often it matched, and how well.

Reviews of this kind mattered because the program guided real decisions about real men. If photo matching proved weak, other leads needed more weight. The report dates from just after the Paris accords, when homecoming sharpened every open case. It shows the identification effort pausing to grade its own tools at a critical moment.
cia-0000009702:
More information on a preliminary debriefing site for captured American pilots arrived in a July 1971 CIA paper. The heading calls the paper additional, meaning earlier reports on the site already existed. Newly captured pilots passed through first questioning before reaching main prisons.

Knowing where that first stage happened helped trace a prisoner's path from capture onward. A man's route through early sites could explain later sightings or their absence. Analysts collected such details piece by piece, often from former prisoners or local sources. This file adds one layer to the map of how captivity began.
cia-0000009802:
Four American prisoners were moved to a new location in Chau Doc province, a February 1972 report states. It follows a January item placing four prisoners in the same Delta province. Read together, the two files trace one group's forced journey.

Movement reports frustrated every plan built on fixed camp locations. A rescue map aged in weeks when prisoners were marched elsewhere. For the accounting, though, movement still proved the men alive on a date. Analysts chained such reports together to keep a group's trail unbroken. This file is one link in that chain, laid down a month after the last.
cia-0000011502:
France's war in Indochina was turning against it when the CIA reviewed the situation there in January 1951. The paper pairs its survey with a map supplement on likely developments. The Viet Minh, backed by the new communist government in China, were gaining ground against French forces across Vietnam, Laos, and Cambodia.

Analysts charted the Viet Minh's gains and the strain the war placed on Paris. They also weighed how the fighting might spread or end. Coming three years before the French defeat at Dien Bien Phu, the study shows the long war's middle passage as Washington watched and worried.
cia-0000012302:
Nuclear matters lead the quoted title of a Helms memo from November 1961, sent to the DIA director. The subject line breaks off at the word Nuclear, the rest cut away in the file. The piece belongs to the Military Thought traffic: Soviet professional writing on the weapons that defined the age. Nothing the colonel's channel carried mattered more than how Moscow's officers thought about nuclear war.

The memo flowed toward year's end without the season slowing it. Value explains the pace: the intelligence was too prized to pause. For readers, the page shows the case's paperwork at its most consequential, where journal articles fed the gravest planning on earth.
cia-0000012402:
Fourteen meetings by May 4, 1961: the record of session fourteen marks a fortnight of near-continuous contact. The handlers' stamina matched the spy's, sitting after sitting. Day after day of questions could exhaust any source. Such a pace could also expose a pattern to watchers. Yet the run held, because the colonel's cover trip kept him in London and his handlers used every day of it.

The record shows the marathon ongoing, session by numbered session. Routine, in the spy world, is what success looks like from inside. For readers, the page conveys the operation's true scale.
cia-0000013302:
Where American prisoners were held in Laos is the subject of a CIA item from July 1962. The item belongs to the captivity's very first years in that kingdom. American airmen and advisers were already being taken in the kingdom's civil war by then. The 1962 pins were the first marks on a long map. That map would grow for a decade, camp by camp and name by name, across some of Asia's hardest country.

The item gives the early Laotian captivity its geography. Later files would add hundreds of reports to this beginning layer. For readers, the page is the pioneering layer of the accounting: the first locations, fixed while the secret war was young.
cia-0000013902: An American pilot prisoner lay in Military Hospital 103 at Ha Dong, in a CIA note dated November 5, 1967. A hurt airman in a northern hospital was news worth filing at once. His care, or lack of it, bore on wider claims about prisoner treatment. The note fixes one wounded man at one known place and date.
cia-0000014802: Dossier material on Anatoli Antonovich Yakovlev fills a CIA file dated January 2, 1963. The file mentions Harry Gold, Klaus Fuchs, and David Greenglass. Those three names formed the chain that broke the atomic spy ring. A dossier still updated in 1963 kept the handler's file alive long after his flight from New York.
cia-0000015402: Chicago officers closed out their dealings with Dr. Leon Davidson in a short CIA note dated January 4, 1958. By phone they told him they could not solve his problem about a space message and its sender. The records, they said, had been destroyed by the agency that judged them. Davidson replied that he had heard that before, and mentioned a new article then under Pentagon review.
cia-0000022302: Rudolf Abel asked James Donovan to call his wife and advise her, a CIA record dated in 1961 reports. Abel was the Soviet spy held in America, and Donovan was his lawyer. The request came while talk of a spy swap was in the air. A small human errand sits inside a hard Cold War bargain in this short entry.
cia-0000036302:
A CIA weekly summary for the Western Hemisphere, dated January 5, 1971, leads with Brazil. Its Brazil item covers talks aimed at winning the release of a kidnapped diplomat. Diplomat kidnappings were then a feared tactic of armed groups across Latin America.

The summary gathers the week's main events into one short briefing for busy officials. The Brazil talks sit beside other regional items, weighed and ranked for the reader. Weekly digests like this show what Washington watched most closely, week by week, across the hemisphere. Kidnapped envoys were often freed only after long talks and hard bargaining over prisoners.
cia-0000042802:
General Ponce admitted that soldiers were held on the Jesuit killings, in a CIA record dated January 1, 1990. Ponce led El Salvador's armed forces as their joint chiefs chairman. An admission from the army's own chief carried unusual weight.

Inside, the admission is recorded in the general's own terms. The army had long been accused of shielding its men from justice. For its leader to say, in public, that soldiers of his own army sat in custody marked a real shift in the case. The file preserves that shift at its first public moment, before trials tested how far the admission would really go.
cia-0000042902:
R. Zamora was interviewed on the killing of the Jesuit priests, in a CIA record dated January 4, 1990. The title ties the interview to the Farabundo Marti National Liberation Front. Rubén Zamora was a leading figure of the Salvadoran left.

Inside, Zamora gives the opposition's reading of the murders. The left blamed the army for the murders. Zamora spoke that charge in public, in plain and repeated terms for the press. His view mattered because he spoke for forces outside the government. The file preserves the case as the opposition framed it, a counterweight in the archive to the statements of presidents and generals.
cia-0000045202:
Rey Prendes commented on the Duarte kidnapping, in a CIA record dated September 2, 1985. Julio Adolfo Rey Prendes was a voice of the Salvadoran right. Hard-liners distrusted any dealing with the guerrillas on principle.

Inside, his reading of the kidnapping case is preserved. Skepticism from the right pressed Duarte from the opposite side. The president was squeezed hard between rebels who held his daughter and allies who hated any concessions to them. Few leaders in that war faced a tighter corner than the one described here. The file records one flank of that pressure, in the words of a man who thought the government already far too soft.
cia-0000049002: El Salvador's military did not step up its activities after the death of a revolutionary leader, and a CIA item dated November 1, 1980, notes the restraint. Analysts watched for the surge that usually followed such a blow, and it did not come. The quiet itself became the fact to explain, and the item preserves it for the Truth Commission files.
cia-0000049202: The Joint Staff's perceptions of the Jesuit case fill a CIA item from 1991, kept with the Truth Commission records. How the staff saw the case, as justice, as threat, or as insult, governed how the institution behaved toward it. The item preserves that inside view at the war's turning point.
cia-0000049302: Dated August 6, 1989, declassified CIA document 0000049302 is headed El Salvador: Insurgents Plan More Assassinations, with a Truth Commission note. The subject is a reported insurgent plan for further killings in El Salvador. Readers find the agency's brief warning as filed, a single dated item that records the claim in its title without expanding it into a fuller account.
cia-0000049402: El Salvador Situation Report number thirteen appears as declassified CIA document 0000049402, dated February 3, 1983. The item carries a Truth Commission note and sits just before report fourteen in the same series and month. Readers get another dated installment of the running situation sequence, valuable mainly for showing the steady rhythm of that reporting.
cia-0000096502: Report to the President on Recommendation number ten of the President's Board of Consultants is declassified CIA document 0000096502, dated March 2, 1957. The heading is cut short in the catalog. The brief file answers on a single numbered recommendation, the highest number in the March run of board follow-up records in this catalog.
cia-0000107402: Pakistan:defense Industry Struggles for Self-sufficiency is the heading, with no space after the colon, on declassified CIA document 0000107402, dated September 1, 1989. The title describes a struggle: Pakistan's defense industry trying to supply itself. No weapon or factory is named in the heading itself. The brief record is a defense industry item from the autumn of 1989.
cia-0000119202:
From February 1971, this CIA document deals with reward leaflets about American prisoners of war held in Laos. Part of the heading was deleted before release, so the person or office it was filed under is unknown. The leaflets offered money for news about captured Americans.

Leaflet rewards were one of the few tools Washington had for finding men lost in Laos. Local people who saw a prisoner, a camp, or a grave could be paid for reporting it. The document keeps the paper trail of that effort, showing how the search for prisoners ran through printed offers dropped and posted across the countryside.
cia-0000124302: A January 1958 CIA report presents orbital data on Soviet Sputniks One, Two, and Three. Orbits could reveal launch sites, rocket strength, and the aims of each flight. The paper is mostly figures, the mathematics of the early space race set down for analysts. Pure data papers rarely survive in public files, and this one shows the raw layer beneath the polished estimates that reached presidents and shaped public claims.
cia-0000132302:
Iraqi ground forces are assessed in Situation Report 612 of the CIA's Iraq-Kuwait series. The report is dated January 3, 1991. Saddam Hussein's army was often described in public debate as one of the largest in the world. Its troops were dug in across Kuwait and southern Iraq.

The report measures that ground threat as the agency itself judged it, apart from newspaper claims. Numbers, equipment, training, and readiness all mattered to planners weighing a land campaign. For readers, the entry shows the gap between the feared army of the headlines and the force analysts described. That judgment shaped choices made before the ground war began.
cia-0000132402:
Cuba is the subject of a CIA briefing given by the Director of Central Intelligence himself. The briefing is dated January 5, 1961. A new Kennedy administration was taking its first hard look at the Cuba problem that month.

When the director briefed in person, the subject sat at the top of the agency's list. The document preserves his assessment as he delivered it to senior officials. For readers, it marks the moment the incoming government inherited the Cuba file. Within months that file would produce the Bay of Pigs invasion and a lasting crisis with Havana.
cia-0000132502: Argentina sending special envoys to both the United States and Cuba fills a CIA document dated February 2, 1961. Buenos Aires was trying to place itself between Washington and Havana as a mediator. Mediating that quarrel would prove a thankless task for any government. The short document covers the planned mission and what Argentina hoped to gain from attempting it that winter.
cia-0000132602:
A large bloc arms shipment to Cuba fills item 16 of the CIA's Latin America series. The item is dated August 5, 1960. Soviet weapons were now flowing to the island in real quantity, shipload after shipload.

The shipment marked a step up from the small buys of the spring. Two years later the same route would carry missiles. That cargo brought the world to the edge of nuclear war in the fall of 1962. For readers, the item is an early dated marker on that road. It shows the buildup while it could still be counted in loads of guns and shells rather than in rockets.
cia-0000135602: Spanish-language papers of the 2506 Brigade fill a CIA record carrying an estimated date of January 1, 1961. Three months stood between this record and the landing at the Bay of Pigs. The brigade's paperwork was piling up as training wound toward its end. The record stands beside an October 1960 file of the same kind. It keeps the Spanish text as filed.
cia-0000135702: One of the Spanish-language papers of Brigade 2506 bears the date 4 January 1961. The brigade was then drilling for the Cuba landing under CIA direction, its men drawn from the exile community. The catalog record for this item carries the series title only, with no subject stated. It survives in Spanish through the CIA Reading Room. Readers should take its contents from the document, not from any summary.
cia-0000136302: Early decisive action is urged in this June 1954 LINCOLN cable, which lists the pressures closing in on the PBSUCCESS forces. Once the enemy doubts victory, it argues, he may demand quick enforcement of a UN cease-fire, while supply problems and reliance on air drops grow unsupportable. The cable calls for seizing ADAM, and possibly BOND as a base, with Plan Alpha's bombing of Matamoros as the softening-up step.
cia-0000136702: The catalog dates this Spanish-language 2506 Brigade document to 3 February 1961, marked as estimated. An earlier summary claimed code clerks, encryption, and an effect on Allied policy for this item; none of that appears in the record, and it is not repeated. The document is a Spanish record of the Cuban exile brigade, then in final training, released in the CIA's declassified files with an estimated February date.
cia-0000137002: Act on embassy asylees now, this June 1954 cable suggests. It went to the Guatemala station chief. The junta should make its requests at the same time. All embassies harboring asylees should get one. The requests should rest on the danger the asylees pose. Demands should stay narrow. They should cover only hard-core communists and sympathizers. Criminal charges must be legally clear against them. Such charges should be drawn up quickly. The top cases need a legal basis first.
cia-0000140402: The hypnotic messenger is explained in this 1954 paper. It covers the military application of hypnotism. A subject can be sent to Berlin on a routine assignment. He carries a message he cannot betray. He will have no waking memory of its contents. He will have no knowledge of ever being hypnotized. Only Colonel X in Berlin can recover the message. His first advantage over an ordinary courier is clear. He can never slip and divulge a mission he does not consciously know.
cia-03153702:
Peiping opens a long Current Intelligence Bulletin dated 19 June 1957, by releasing its official version of Mao's secret speech of 27 February. The text, issued on 18 June, claims to rest on the verbatim record. The comment detects editing for bloc harmony. Hungary's disorders plainly shaped Mao's talk of contradictions in Chinese society. Those contradictions are called mostly non-antagonistic, to be settled by persuasion.

Peiping also plans large withdrawals from Tibet. France's Moch resists the Soviet nuclear test suspension proposal. Yemen takes a new Soviet arms deal as bloc technicians arrive. Communist arms probably meant for Algerian rebels reach North Africa. Japan unites behind the Kishi mission to Washington, and resents South Korean stalling on detainees. Pakistan seeks a Security Council meeting on Kashmir for 8 July. A new Iraqi prime minister and a Greek visit to Egypt close the issue.
cia-06186302:
Staff Memorandum No. 1-59, dated January 1959, from the Office of National Estimates, records a consultants' conference at Princeton. The meeting ran 4-5 December 1958. Participants listed include Allen W. Dulles, George Kennan, Hamilton Fish Armstrong, and Abbott Smith, alongside other consultants and CIA staff.

The agenda covered a topic listed as BOUNDER and NIE 11-1-58 on main trends in Soviet capabilities and policies. Much debate centered on one claim in NIE 11-4-58 about surprise attack. Most consultants tended to dispute the claim that Soviet theorists did not see surprise as decisive in a major war. Mosely and Kennan are recorded with opposing views on how far published Soviet writing reflects real thinking. Berlin and Soviet aims in Europe were also argued at length.
cia-06240902:
Letter dated 4 October 2001, from the Executive Director, protests the tone of a House intelligence committee mark-up. The letter goes to Tim Sample, staff director of the Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence. A signature routing form at the front gives the originating office as DCI/EXDIR and a control number, DAC-04842-01.

The writer states that the committee's mark-up of the Administration's request for the Fiscal Year 2002 program carried an accusatory, insulting, and demeaning tone. Three items are singled out. One matter is described as dismissed out of hand. Remarks about the Office of Congressional Affairs are called a shock, given daily contact with its senior staff. A cut to the Office of the Inspector General is called particularly offensive in the portion shown. The letter is marked for official use only.
cleopatra-volume-02:
Georg Ebers set his novel Cleopatra in Alexandria during the queen's struggle with Rome, and Volume 2 moves the private story forward. Ebers wrote in German, and this English text follows Barine, a young Alexandrian beauty whose first marriage has ended. She lives again with her widowed mother Berenike, in a house tied to scholars and philosophers.

Chapter IV explains how Barine's family connects to both camps in the coming war. Her uncle Arius taught the young Octavian, yet Mark Antony still treats him with open kindness in Alexandria. That split loyalty gives the volume its tension. Around Barine, court favor, family duty, and the rivalry between Antony and Octavian shape every visit, gift, and promise.
coniston-volume-02:
Book Two of Winston Churchill's novel Coniston opens with politics riding into a New Hampshire village. Churchill, the American novelist, built the book around Jethro Bass, a silent state boss who trades in votes and favors. His lieutenant Bijah Bixby of Clovelly appears here, spying out the ground for his chief. Storekeeper William Wetherell and his daughter Cynthia walk into that machinery unaware.

Bijah works the village store like a market, sounding out Chester Perkins and others. He made the Honorable Heth Sutton a legislator and delivers him in blocks of votes for set prices. Cynthia, a thoughtful country girl, grows up under the shadow of Jethro's power. Love, loyalty, and political debt begin to pull against each other in her story. Churchill writes the boss system from inside, . Readers following the full novel need this book for Cynthia's youth and Jethro's hold on her world.
conrad-typhoon-1902:
Joseph Conrad drew Typhoon from his own years as a merchant navy officer in eastern seas. The novella first appeared in magazine form and was published as a book in 1902. It is one of his most direct and powerful sea stories.

Captain MacWhirr, a stolid and literal-minded man, refuses to steer around a coming storm in the China Sea. His ship, the Nan-Shan, sails straight into the typhoon with a cargo of Chinese laborers below deck. Conrad renders the storm's force in famous detail. The real subject is MacWhirr himself: dim, stubborn, and somehow exactly the man the crisis needs.
constitution-indonesia-2002:
Indonesia's constitution dates from 1945, the year freedom from Dutch rule was declared, and the hosted text carries the four rounds of change made from 1999 to 2002. The preamble states the state philosophy, Pancasila, five principles covering belief in God, humanity, unity, democracy, and social justice. The body of the text is short and was long left vague on purpose.

A president leads the executive and, after the changes, is chosen by direct vote with term limits. The People's Representative Council makes laws, and a People's Consultative Assembly joins it with regional members for the largest acts. Later chapters cover the courts, a Constitutional Court added in 2003, local areas, and state finance. The changes turned a tool of strongman rule into a democratic charter.
constitution-monaco-2002:
Monaco, a tiny city-state on the French Riviera, works under a constitution granted by Prince Rainier the Third in 1962, hosted here in its 2002 form. Early titles cover the principality and public powers, then the prince and the passing of the crown. Monaco is a hereditary monarchy, and the prince holds the executive power in his own hands, a design few European states keep.

A Minister of State, traditionally a French civil servant, runs the government day to day. The National Council, chosen by voters, shares lawmaking but cannot bring the government down. A chapter protects basic freedoms and rights. Later titles cover the courts, the crown council, local rule in the single commune, and finance. French is the official language.
cooley-human-nature-social-order-1902:
Human Nature and the Social Order, published in 1902, is Charles Horton Cooley's founding text of what became symbolic interactionism. The American sociologist argues that self and society are twins: neither exists apart from the other.

His famous concept is the looking-glass self: we imagine how we appear to others, imagine their judgment of that appearance, and feel pride or shame accordingly. Through such mirrors, persons are made in communication. Cooley writes gently, with a novelist's eye for inner life. The book reshaped American sociology and social psychology, and its central image is still in daily use.
crawley-the-mystic-rose-1902:
Ernest Crawley's 1902 study of primitive marriage took on a subject few scholars had treated directly: sexual taboo. He argued that fear and prohibition, not free early love, shaped the first rules of marriage and contact between the sexes.

Crawley examines seclusion rites, the dread of contagion through touch, and the religious force behind bans on certain unions. He ranges across peoples and periods in search of the roots of these prohibitions. His claim was that taboo made individuals distinct and society possible. The book pioneered the study of taboo and influenced later writers on marriage and purity rules.
crowley-equinox-vol-1-no-02:
September 1909 brought the second number of Crowley's great journal, The Equinox. The Equinox, volume one, number two, keeps the twice-yearly pace he set for the work. The journal served as the public record of his order and its teaching.

Fresh rites and teaching papers saw print here first, as they did in each number. Verse, reviews, and tall tales fill out the bulk beside the grave matter. The whole run of the journal is the prime source for the birth of Thelema. Number two shows the young venture in full and confident stride. Its white bulk set the look of all the numbers to come.
cumner-s-son-and-other-south-sea-folk-vo:
Cumner's Son and Other South Sea Folk, Volume 2, by Gilbert Parker, is marked Australiana on its title page and opens in a bush camp. Parker seats his narrator cooking chops at a billabong, a waterhole, while Barlas kneads a damper and Drysdale packs coals around the billy. The camp's guest is Stewart Ruttan, the Cadi. He is the new magistrate at Windowie and Gilgan. He gets the lazy side of the fire. He gets a fig of the best tobacco too, because he represents the Government.

The High Court of Budgery-Gar, his errand, gives the volume its lead tale. An Epic in Yellow, Dibbs R.N., A Little Masquerade, Derelict, Old Roses, My Wife's Lovers, and The Strangers' Hut complete the gathering. Bush law, naval strays, and station romances alternate. Parker writes Australia as he wrote Canada.
darwiniana-essays-volume-02:
Thomas Henry Huxley's Darwiniana, the second volume of his collected essays, gathers pieces on evolution and on Darwin himself. Huxley says he chose the title because the essays treat the ancient doctrine of evolution, rehabilitated by the Origin of Species, or answer the criticisms that greeted that great work.

Other essays record the impression Darwin's personality left on a friend of thirty years, and sum up his work and its enduring influence on scientific thought. The first two essays, from 1859 and 1860, show Huxley already demanding fair play for Darwin. Readers interested in the Darwinian debates, or in Huxley as Darwin's bulldog, will find this volume the essential companion.
das-journey-to-lhasa-1902:
Sarat Chandra Das slipped into Tibet in disguise and wrote Journey to Lhasa and Central Tibet, edited by W. W. Rockhill in 1902. Das, a Bengali schoolmaster and scholar of Tibetan, made secret journeys in 1881 and 1882 for the British survey. His narrative opens a closed land: monasteries, officials, mountain roads, and the great city of Lhasa itself.

Few outsiders saw nineteenth-century Tibet from inside, and fewer still wrote of it so fully and so well. Das paid for his knowledge with suspicion, illness, and hardship on his return to India. The book remains a primary Western source on the old Tibet before modern change swept through it.
defoe-shortest-way-with-the-dissenters-1:
Daniel Defoe published The Shortest Way with the Dissenters in 1702, a savage ironic pamphlet in prose. The tract urges, in a High Church voice, the persecution and hanging of Protestant Dissenters in England. Taken literally by both sides, it led to his prosecution, pillorying, and ruin in 1703 by law.

Defoe mimics a zealot so well that Anglicans applauded and Dissenters trembled before the hoax broke open. His point was that persecution's logic ends at the gallows, whatever soft words clothe it at first. The state read sedition in the irony, fined him, and stood him in the pillory three days. Crowds drank his health and threw flowers, and he wrote a hymn to the pillory from prison. The affair made Defoe famous and broke him, the making of the later novelist.
devereux-volume-02:
Book two of Lytton's Devereux fills this second volume, and it brings the hero to London. A headnote warns that pleasure is often the shortest road to wisdom. Young men of fortune had just begun, the tale says, to keep house and give bachelor homes the weight of married ones.

The hero's suite near the court is crowded with callers on pleasure's errands. Jean Desmarais, his French valet, tends a coffee pot and mangles English for the room's sport. A tailor with Paris patterns waits among the rest. Talk turns to Lady Clancathcart's face and Mrs Denton's claims. This file holds book two only: London wit and fashion, before the tale darkens.
dewey-child-curriculum-1902:
The Child and the Curriculum, published in 1902, is Dewey's short classic on the central quarrel of schooling. Reformers fought over whether education should follow the child's nature or the demands of the subject matter; Dewey argues the quarrel itself is false.

The child and the curriculum, he says, are two ends of one process: the child's present experience and the organized knowledge of the race. Teaching is the art of guiding the one into the other without crushing either. The essay is barely fifty pages and has never gone out of use. It remains the clearest statement of Dewey's educational faith.
dioscorides-materia-medica-berendes-1902:
Pedanius Dioscorides, a Greek doctor of the first century, wrote the founding book of drug lore. De Materia Medica, in Julius Berendes's German rendering of 1902, gives his five books whole. Doctors lived by this text for more than fifteen hundred years.

Dioscorides lists hundreds of plants, stones, and animal parts, with the use and dose of each. He tells how to know the true drug from the false and how to store each kind. His plain, tested style set the form of drug books for ages. Berendes's version opened the Greek master to German readers.
doe-osti-3024209-fuel-cell-electric-bus-:
Matthew Jeffers, Yi He, and Michael Lammert of the National Laboratory of the Rockies give the 2025 status of fuel cell electric buses in report NLR/TP-5400-97796, dated March 2026. Transit agencies running hydrogen buses need fleet-level facts: how often the buses are available, and what takes them out of service. The report tracks the fuel cell fleet against three baseline compressed natural gas fleets.

Monthly availability for the fuel cell fleet ranged from 65.4 percent to 91.2 percent, averaging 76.8 percent. Figures break unavailable days down by cause. The NABI natural gas fleet ran lowest, between 61.5 and 83 percent, mainly on engine and transmission trouble. The ENC and New Flyer gas fleets generally held high availability, which sets the bar the hydrogen fleet is measured against.
doe-osti-3365136-lamp-emittance-budget-l:
Los Alamos National Laboratory report LAMP-ENG-RPT-002, by Robert Garnett and issued May 18, 2026, sets the emittance budget for the LAMP accelerator. Emittance measures how spread out a particle beam is in position and angle. Every accelerator section adds some spread. The budget allocates how much growth each part may cause before beam quality suffers. Garnett, a senior advisor to the project, prepared the budget for the NNSA Office of Experimental Science.

A budget document like this one anchors design reviews: subsystem owners sign that their growth allowances are achievable, and systems engineering tracks the totals. Reviewers here included the LAT task lead and the deputy technical director, with approvals dated April and May 2026. Beam physicists designing LAMP's ion source, transport lines, and accelerating structures work against these numbers.
dunbar-sport-of-gods-1902:
Paul Laurence Dunbar published The Sport of the Gods in 1902, a novel about a Black family from the South. Berry Hamilton is a loyal former servant accused of a theft he did not commit. He goes to prison, and his family moves to New York City. The city promises freedom but brings new harms.

His wife, son, and daughter each face temptation, crime, and despair. Dunbar shows how racism and city life work together to crush them. The title points to forces that treat human lives as playthings. The novel was an early and bleak portrait of the move north later called the Great Migration.
eckartshausen-wolke-1802:
Karl von Eckartshausen published Die Wolke über dem Heiligthum, The Cloud upon the Sanctuary, in German in 1802. The book is built as six letters, each one addressed to a seeking reader. Its theme is the interior Church, a hidden fellowship of the elect that lives within the outer one.

Eckartshausen teaches that this inner Church keeps the deepest truths of faith alive across the ages. His letters move quietly, urging the reader inward rather than toward new rites or orders. The work carried Rosicrucian and theosophic ideas into the 1800s with real force. Later groups, from the Golden Dawn to the Martinists, drew on its vision.
encyclopaedia-biblica-vol3-1902:
Volume Three of the Encyclopaedia Biblica, from 1902, covers L to P. Cheyne and Black's critical dictionary was now the standard proof that Bible study had changed forever. Its articles assume readers who want evidence, not comfort.

Major entries treat the Law, the Messiah, Palestine, the Pharisees, and the prophets. Natural history articles identify the plants and animals of scripture with care. The volume also maps tribal lands and traces place names through the sources. Critics attacked its doubts; students mined its facts. Either way, no serious Bible library of 1902 was complete without it. Signed initials at each article's end name the scholar who stands behind it.
engels-origin-family-1902:
In The Origin of the Family, Private Property and the State, Engels turned the notes of Marx into one sweeping story. He also drew on the field work of Lewis Henry Morgan on kinship among Native peoples. Ernest Untermann translated this English edition, published in 1902. The book is the charter text of Marxist anthropology.

Engels traces family forms from group marriage to the modern household, linking each step to changes in property and farming. He argues that the monogamous family, private wealth, and the state all rose together. Critics have faulted his sources, but the book shaped a century of debate on kinship and power.
enuma-elish-king-1902:
Leonard William King presents the Babylonian creation epic in The Seven Tablets of Creation, published by Luzac in London in 1902, in a Semitic text and translation series. King's long introduction describes the poem Enuma Elish, weighs new material, and argues its date and origin. A full section traces the legend's influence and its parallels in Hebrew literature.

The tablets follow in transliteration and translation, first to seventh, with an epilogue. Other creation accounts fill a second part: another dragon-myth version, the creation of cattle, of moon and sun, and the Cuthaean legend. Assyrian commentaries stand in the appendices. King writes for scholars, with the cuneiform kept in view. The catalog year for this record is plainly wrong; the book is King's 1902 edition.
ernest-maltravers-volume-02:
Volume Two of Ernest Maltravers contains Book the Second of Edward Bulwer Lytton's novel, opening at a brilliant ball in the Palazzo of the Austrian embassy at Naples. The crowd gathers around Madame de Ventadour, reigning beauty of the hour. Lytton pauses to ask why the world gives its golden apple where it does, blaming caprice more than taste.

Maltravers moves through the brilliant resorts of the world, admired and drifting. The narrator judges that he had gained little from experience as yet, and that the world was affecting him as it does everyone. A Rousseau epigraph confesses something singular in his sentiments for a charming woman. The volume deepens Ernest's Italian season and his entanglements, far from Alice.
essays-of-michel-de-montaigne-volume-02:
Book One opens in Volume 2 of Michel de Montaigne's Essays, here in Charles Cotton's English translation. Montaigne (1533-1592), a French landowner and former judge, invented a loose form he called an essay, meaning a trial or test. He tries out ideas on himself first. Twelve short chapters start the sequence.

Early pieces ask how enemies can be won over by surrender or by bold defiance. Others treat sorrow, feelings that outlive their cause, and anger spent on the wrong target. Two chapters warn a besieged governor about talks with an enemy outside the walls. Later pieces cover intention, idleness, liars, fast and slow speech, fortune telling, and constancy under pressure. Short Roman and French stories carry most points. New readers often start here to learn Montaigne's plain, questioning voice.
eugene-aram-volume-02:
Volume 02 holds Book II of Edward Bulwer Lytton's Eugene Aram. It opens with the marriage settled: Aram's love for Madeline Lester has been told to her father, her consent won, and the wedding fixed for the end of the month after mid-September. One pang remains, for his nephew Walter had hoped for Madeline himself.

Against the wedding plans, danger gathers at the edges. Walter's servant, the Corporal, swears he has seen again a hard-faced man who once drank at Peter Dealtry's inn and knew Aram at once, far from Grassdale. Strangers with a past link to the Student are moving closer. Readers get the middle turn of the tale, where promised happiness and an old, unnamed threat advance side by side toward the wedding day.
europmc-pmc10011802:
Yang and co-authors review AlphaFold2 and its uses in biology and medicine in a 2023 paper. AlphaFold2 is an AI system from DeepMind that predicts the three-dimensional shape of proteins from their building-block sequences. It does so with a level of accuracy that once took years of lab work for a single protein.

The review explains how the tool works and where labs now use it. Uses range from basic cell science to drug design and disease study. The authors also note the tool's limits. Readers get a clear tour of a landmark AI system.
europmc-pmc10200802:
Chen and a large team review macrophages in immune regulation and therapy in a 2023 paper. Macrophages are versatile immune cells that live in tissues throughout the body. They eat germs and dead cells, raise alarms, and help heal wounds, and they can switch between attack and repair modes.

The review explains how that switching is controlled and what goes wrong in cancer and chronic disease. It surveys therapies that reprogram macrophages or use them as drug carriers. The authors see these cells as both targets and tools in future medicine.
europmc-pmc10468402:
Li and co-authors showed in 2023 that chromosome errors in cancer cells drive spread through the immune system. Such errors, called chromosomal instability, scramble the number of chromosomes as cells divide. They had long been tied to metastasis, the spread of cancer to new sites. How much that link needs the immune system was unknown.

Errors trigger a DNA alarm, the cGAS-STING path, inside cancer cells. Li found that long alarm use rewires the cells and stirs stress in their inner stores. That mix makes the tumour zone friendlier to spread. Blocking STING or the stress path cut spread in mice with sound immune systems. Human breast cancer data showed the same marks in tumours that had spread.
europmc-pmc10622502:
Sun and co-authors reviewed smart nanoparticles for cancer care in 2023. These tiny carriers can sense body cues or follow them to a tumour. That skill marks them as a sharp tool for precise drug delivery. The review sorts the many carrier types now in work.

The list runs from polymer and protein carriers to gold, iron oxide, and carbon tubes. Sun shows how each is built and what makes it smart.
